title: Grain-Boundary-Engineered La2CuO4 Perovskite Nanobamboos for Efficient CO2 Reduction Reaction

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Cu-based CO2 reduction catalysts need high Faradaic efficiency toward C2 products such as C2H4. Engineering twin boundaries into La2CuO4 perovskite should steer CO2RR selectivity toward C2H4.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/forming), n6 (PRC/synthesis)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: La2CuO4 NBs are bamboo-like chains of single grains joined at necks, keeping a rugged-surfaced 3D fiber network. The NB necks are twin boundaries, the NR junctions are ordinary grain boundaries, and bulk La2CuO4 has no boundaries.
states.detail: Absorbed: n7 (STR/microstructure/shape), n8 (STR/defect/extended), n9 (STR/phase/lattice), n10 (STR/chemistry/bonding). Premises: A low calcination heating rate gives a surface energy that favours boundary formation, while a high rate speeds PVP decomposition and crystal growth to a bulk solid

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: CO-related intermediates bind more strongly on La2CuO4 NBs and NRs than on bulk La2CuO4. Strain at the twin boundaries lengthens Cu-O and Cu-La bonds, strengthening CO* binding and promoting C-C coupling to C2H4.
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (PRP/value), n12 (MEC/pathway), n13 (PRP/descriptor), n14 (PRP/value), n15 (MEC/identification), n25 (MEC/pathway). Premises: In temperature-programmed desorption a higher desorption peak temperature means a stronger adsorbate-surface bond; CO2 reduction to C2 products proceeds by C-C coupling of adsorbed CO intermediates, which requires CO* to stay bound to the surface

states.title: Performance state
states.head: La2CuO4 NBs reach an FE for C2H4 of 60% at -1.0 V vs RHE and keep C2H4 the largest product from -1.0 to -1.3 V. Bulk La2CuO4 gives an FE for CO of 91% at -1.0 V vs RHE and produces no C2H4 at any potential

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Boundary engineering switches CO2RR selectivity of one perovskite: strained twin boundaries give C2H4, boundary-free bulk gives CO

nodes.title: IR:DRIFTS, F5, F6
nodes.head: Over 12 h the NB current density drifts from -2.8 to -4.0 mA/cm2 and the bulk holds near -6.3, while FE points stay at 55-62% C2H4 and about 85% CO. The Cu L-edge spectra of all three La2CuO4 samples reproduce the CuO reference peak near 931 eV and lack the Cu2O and Cu-foil features
